content: Professional courtesy refers to the longstanding tradition among physicians of not charging one another for the medical treatment of their family members. This practice was originally intended to discourage physicians from treating their own family members as patients, thereby avoiding potential ethical and emotional conflicts. Additionally, it served to strengthen professional bonds and mutual respect among physicians. The origins of this custom can be traced back to the time of Hippocrates, emphasizing its deep historical roots. While primarily associated with the medical profession, the concept of professional courtesy has also been observed in other fields. For example, police officers may refrain from issuing tickets to fellow officers, and lawyers are expected to demonstrate ethical behavior toward one another in their professional interactions. In the medical field, this tradition continues to be respected in countries such as the United States and Egypt. However, some prominent physicians may choose to disregard this practice, often with the intention of encouraging their colleagues to seek care from other, potentially less expensive, healthcare providers.
